about: Sources Civgraph fetched and compared figure by figure with its own contest files (origin web-check in data/database/election-provenance.json). checked is true only where every compared figure agreed; otherwise check and disagreements say what differed. Citations and comparison notes only: no text is copied from the sources. Read by scripts/build-election-provenance.mjs.

batches.note: The 203 contests that had no source: NI local government (ARK; one Irish News), NI Forum 1996 (ARK), Westminster by-elections and European 2019 (ARK), Dáil 2014 (electionsireland.org), ROI referendums (Department of Housing CSVs on data.gov.ie; electionsireland.org).

Republic of Ireland local elections (mainly 1985-2009, plus other years where pages existed), checked in a normal headless browser against electionsireland.org (the import source) and irelandelection.com (independent). Pages with no result table, or nothing to compare, are not recorded. BBC pages were not fetched: its robots.txt disallows the agent.

Republic of Ireland referendums: every constituency file and national result compared with the Department of Housing's per-referendum datasets (opendata.housing.gov.ie, listed on data.gov.ie), corrected where they differed and given total poll and spoilt votes; five national figures settled with referendum.ie's result summaries. Also the 2026 Dublin Central and Galway West by-elections, checked against the official results volumes.

Dail contests 1948-1977 compared with the constituency results printed in the Irish Press, Irish Independent and Cork Examiner (Irish Newspaper Archives, OCR read by Civgraph): candidates, first preferences and members elected; transfers not compared. Citations only.

Presidential elections and Republic of Ireland local contests (1974-1985) compared with newspaper reports in the Irish Newspaper Archives. Checked where every compared figure agrees; partial checks say what was compared. Citations only.

Westminster contests in Ireland, 1885-1922, compared with newspaper reports in the British Newspaper Archive (OCR, with page images read for the by-elections whose figures differed). Unopposed returns are confirmed by a report naming the member as returned. Citations only.

Winners, parties and by-election causes in NI contests compared with the Chronology of Major Events in Sydney Elliott and W. D. Flackes, Northern Ireland: A Political Directory 1968-1999 (Blackstaff Press, 1999), read from scans (pp. 1-39 and 88-111). The book gives no vote figures, so only members returned and causes are compared. Citations only; no text from the book is held.

The Belfast Gazette's lists of members returned (Crown Office for Northern Ireland: the Parliament of Northern Ireland, general elections and by-elections, and Westminster seats in Northern Ireland), read from the Gazette's own text layer by scripts/gazette/extract_election_notices.py and matched to each contest by scripts/gazette/record_gazette_provenance.py. Checked where every Civgraph winner is named in the return and no entry disagrees; the Gazette prints no votes, so the check is of the members returned, not the figures. Crown copyright, Open Government Licence.

Party-internal contests (leadership and nomination ballots) loaded with the facts model (docs/facts-model.md), checked against a second source for what Elliott and Flackes (1999) leaves out: the day of a contest it dates only by month, and the identity of a candidate. Citations and comparison notes only.

records.title: March 1995 Ulster Unionist Party leadership election (Wikipedia)
records.check: The article dates the challenge to the Ulster Unionist Council meeting of 18 March 1995 and gives Lee Reynolds 88 votes, as Elliott and Flackes (1999) does.
